extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalists, and researchers studying news selection, framing, and homepage placement
extracted.subtask_description: Analyze how institutionally authorized sources ('primary definers') shape which events become news, the frames used, and the resulting moral panic dynamics; apply these criteria to evaluate news selection and homepage placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Definer Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'primary definer' is an actor whose institutional position licenses them to be the first to define a situation in the news — police chiefs, judges, government ministers, recognized experts. Reporters' objectivity rituals require named, authoritative sources; primary definers reliably supply them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: the primary definer's framing becomes the initial frame of the story; subsequent voices appear as secondary responses; counter-frames must labor to displace the established frame. Use this to evaluate whose definition anchors a story and how that initial frame structures subsequent coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Anchoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Events become reportable when an authorized institutional actor speaks about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events not yet processed by primary definers struggle to enter the news. When assessing news selection, check whether a story surfaced only after an institutional spokesperson commented or released information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame Inheritance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a primary definer labels an event (e.g., 'mugging,' 'riot,' 'extremist attack,' 'epidemic'), that label propagates across coverage; alternative labels look partisan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate headlines and lead paragraphs for inherited terminology from institutions; alternative framings face credibility/partisanship costs and must overcome default labels to gain traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source Hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a hierarchy of authorized speakers (Police > activists; ministers > NGOs; CEOs > workers) that determines whose perspective shapes news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check which actors are given priority and citation in stories. The ordering and prominence of sources (who is named first, who provides the statistics) is itself a criterion for assessing bias toward institutional perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers from primary definer institutions (police statistics, agency reports) get reported as fact; non-institutional counts must justify themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether institutional statistics are presented unproblematically as authoritative and whether grassroots or alternative data are required to 'prove' themselves; note how this affects perceived magnitude of problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral Panic Amplification Cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: A cyclical process: Primary definers identify a 'problem' → Media report it using primary-definer frames → Public concern rises; politicians demand 'action' → Police prioritize the issue, generating more recorded cases → Media report the rise as confirmation → Loop continues, manufacturing a 'crisis.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this sequence to trace feedback loops between institutions, media coverage, public reaction, and official responses. When evaluating time-series or placement data, look for mutually reinforcing increases in coverage and recorded incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification (stage of moral panic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary definers name a new threat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate first public characterizations of an event: who named the threat and what terminology was used. Early naming often determines subsequent framing and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylization (stage of moral panic)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for reductionist or stereotyped portrayals that simplify complex social categories into emblematic types; assess how such stylization shapes audience perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolization (stage of moral panic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific symbols come to stand in for the threat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify recurring symbols (places, images, objects, terms) used to shorthand the threat. These symbols consolidate and circulate the frame across stories and platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distortion (stage of moral panic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics and incidents are reported in inflammatory ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether figures or incidents are presented out of context, exaggerated, or selectively highlighted to increase perceived severity; examine headline framing and selective reporting patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplification (stage of moral panic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing coverage amplifies the perceived threat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure repetition, placement prominence, and cross-outlet propagation that increase salience. Repetition across outlets and over time serves to normalize the frame as an urgent public issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for Action (stage of moral panic)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate coverage for calls to action, policy responses, or rhetoric from officials linking media attention to demands for enforcement or legislation; such demand legitimizes institutional responses and closes the amplification loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime/Risk Story Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics with active primary-definer apparatus (police, public health, security agencies) generate steady news flow; topics without such apparatus do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing news agendas or homepage composition, expect overrepresentation of issues that have institutional reporting mechanisms; absent institutional sources, comparable issues may be undercovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterhegemonic Stories Pay an Evidentiary Tax
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting that contradicts primary-definer framing requires extra sourcing, slowing or suppressing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess differential sourcing burdens: alternative frames often need more corroboration or expert backing to be treated as legitimate, which affects timeliness and prominence on homepages.

rubrics_metrics.name: News-cycle Entrenchment
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a frame is established, subsequent coverage reproduces it; novel frames are filtered out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how initial frames persist across follow-ups and how editorial routines favor replication of established narratives; check whether attempts at reframing are marginalized or appended as secondary perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical Testability on Homepage Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories using primary-definer terminology in headlines (police-supplied labels, agency-supplied statistics) should achieve higher placement than stories using alternative terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical test: measure headline language and placement rank on homepages; compare prevalence and position of institutionally framed stories versus counter-framed stories to operationalize the primary-definer hypothesis.
